headline: Natural selection is differential survival—traits that help reproduction become more common
universal_truth: What works spreads; what doesn't, doesn't; the environment selects for fit
fun_facts: Darwin didn't invent the idea of evolution—he explained the mechanism: natural selection
Selection can produce rapid change—peppered moths went from mostly light to mostly dark in decades during industrial pollution
Antibiotic resistance evolves in bacteria within days—selection working in real-time
discussion_questions: What 'selection pressures' act on you—in career, relationships, life?
How do you adapt to fit your environment versus change your environment?
What traits are being selected for in your context?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Some individuals reproduce more than others. Their traits become more common. Over time, the population changes—not through planning, but through differential success. This is natural selection: the mechanism of evolution.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Natural selection has no intention—it's just what works spreading. Yet it produces remarkably designed-seeming results. What does this teach us?

options.text: Selection shows that design can emerge from trial and error—you don't need a plan if you iterate, select what works, and repeat; success compounds
options.response: Yes. Evolution has no goal, yet produces incredible complexity. The lesson: try variations, keep what works, discard what doesn't. Iterate toward fitness without needing to know the destination.

options.text: Selection is just survival of the fittest
options.response: 'Fittest' means fitting the environment, not strongest—it's about fit, not force...

q1.title: Fit Not Strong
q1.script: 'Fittest' means best fit to environment—not strongest. A well-camouflaged moth is more fit than a strong one in a forest. The environment defines what counts as success.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Fit Not Strong"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: No Foresight
q2.script: Selection has no foresight—it favors what works now, not what might work later. This creates vulnerabilities; what's fit today may not fit tomorrow. Short-term optimization can create long-term fragility.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Applied Selection
q3.script: You can apply selection thinking: try many approaches, keep what works, discard what doesn't. Markets do this. Science does this. Personal experimentation does this. Selection is a learning mechanism.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What works spreads; what doesn't, doesn't. The environment selects for fit. Understand the selection pressures you face.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 267. Tomorrow, we'll explore animals running out of time—endangered species. Until then, consider what selection pressures shape your choices.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Selection Pressure Analysis - What's Being Selected For?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify selection pressures in your environment
growTrack.activity: What 'selection pressures' act in your context—work, relationships, life? What traits are being rewarded? What's being punished? Understanding selection helps you either adapt to fit or change your environment.
